title: Maintaining Correct Slope on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Maintaining proper slope on horizontal drainage piping is critical for waste transport. If a drain line has insufficient fall, water moves too slowly, leaving solid waste behind to accumulate and cause clogs. Conversely, an excessive slope allows liquids to rush ahead, leaving solids stranded in the pipe. A standard minimum slope for branch drains up to 3 inches is typically 1/4 inch per foot. Always verify local plumbing code requirements and support pipes properly using approved hangers to prevent belly sags where waste can settle over time.
